text:
Jen Support: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting an increase in 5xx + timeouts after the canary rolled out at ~09:00 UTC. Also seeing billing anomalies (duplicate charge attempts). Anyone oncall?

Liam SRE: I'm on it. Can you paste an example req id and customer id?

Jen Support: sure — cust=acme-inc, req=01H7X2ZQ9Y, sample error: `gateway timeout` then a retry that succeeded but produced two invoice lines.

Jen Support: repro steps from customer: 1) POST /v1/generate with api_key header 2) 30s wait -> 504 3) client retries -> 200 and invoice charged again (they're on per-token billing).

Nora Eng: tagging this with the canary we flipped — we rolled `auth_token_rotation=true` to 10% at 09:00. @Liam SRE could that affect our gateway auth path?

Liam SRE: Possibly. I'm seeing a spike in backend 5xx where the auth service returns 500 during validation then gateway treats as backend failure. Pulling logs now.

Liam SRE: log snippet: ```
2026-03-17T09:02:14Z auth-validator ERROR "panic validating token" trace=01H7X2ZQ9Y
2026-03-17T09:02:14Z gateway WARN Backend returned 502 for req=01H7X2ZQ9Y
2026-03-17T09:02:15Z billing INFO charge_attempt cust=acme-inc req=01H7X2ZQ9Y status=queued
2026-03-17T09:02:45Z billing INFO charge_attempt cust=acme-inc req=01H7X2ZQ9Y status=processed
```

Nora Eng: That auth log matches a codepath where the rotation code falls back to legacy signer if a feature flag is true. We added a canary toggle but a config mismatch could cause intermittent panics.

Maya Ops: Recommend immediate rollback of the canary toggle to stop traffic hitting the new codepath. We can also block 10% traffic with routing override. Which is faster?

Liam SRE: Rollback via config is quick. I'll flip the canary flag back to false in 2 mins and route canary traffic to stable to avoid retries.

Nora Eng: Pushing hotfix to remove the fallback that triggers panic in edge cases. Will post PR link after.

Liam SRE: Running: `rdctl feature set auth_token_rotation false --env=prod --scope=canary` (exec 09:10:12Z)

deploy-bot: feature toggle update recorded — auth_token_rotation set to false for canary at 3112346132 by liam_sre

Liam SRE: Also applied routing override: `traffic-router set-route /v1/generate stable` (exec 09:10:45Z). Watching 5xx rate.

Jen Support: Noting customer-facing message: "We've rolled back a recent canary that caused some requests to time out. If you saw duplicate billing lines from retries, we're investigating refunds — DM me cust ids." :thumbsup:

Ash Billing: Please DM list of affected customers. We'll pause automatic retry billing for those req ids and open refund cases. Need cust ids + invoice ids.

Jen Support: DM'd Ash the list (acme-inc, beta-apps, sparkly-ai) and sample invoice ids.

Liam SRE: Metrics update: 5xx rate dropped from 4.6% -> 0.7% within 3m of rollback. Latency back to baseline.

Maya Ops: Confirmed no further duplicate charges observed in logs for those req ids after routing override.

Nora Eng: PR #4982 created to remove the fallback; test suite added for rotated tokens. We'll schedule a safe canary with circuit-breaker + no-auto-retry billing window.

Liam SRE: Postmortem action items: 1) Harden auth validator against null signer cases, 2) add canary telemetry alert for auth validator 5xx spikes, 3) block billing retry if prior request returned non-2xx within window — assigned.

Jen Support: Thanks all. I'll update the open support tickets and notify customers that we're issuing refunds where applicable.

Ash Billing: Acknowledged — will send refund confirmations as cases close.

Nora Eng: Leaving follow-up in #postmortems with links to logs and PR.

Liam SRE: Incident resolved, moving to follow-up. :white_check_mark:
